purpose: Pre-registered confirmation plan: v6-v11 all selected methods, arms, comparisons and seeds on the SAME validation split, so their p-values are exploratory. This manifest freezes the main comparisons, endpoints, seed count and statistics BEFORE any WikiText-103 test-split evaluation, and the confirmation data (wiki.test.raw) has never been read by any earlier phase. v2: the seed count was raised 6 -> 12 and the manifest gained a machine-checkable binding block and a scope declaration; the revision was made strictly BEFORE any test-split evaluation (no P5T result has ever existed -- no results_lm_test/ record, no commit touching the test split), which is the only condition under which a pre-registration may be revised without selection bias. v3 (2026-10-19): aligned the stamp with CODE_SEMANTICS v11.128, pinned the implementation binding (all four frozen arms run the per-row RoPE loop, so eager_batch=false), pinned the per-arm mlp_ratio, disclosed the parameter-vs-compute mismatch and the decision rule, and added a zero-GPU plan self-check. Again strictly BEFORE any test-split access. v5 adds the sink-matched dense and no-sink csa arms, replaces the fixed-hash random control with a per-(seed, layer) seeded draw, and raises the test slice to 48 documents; still before any test access.
implementation_binding_note: eager_batch is false for every frozen arm. All four arms have rope=True, and HybridAttentionRoPE.forward routes every CSA layer through the per-row _single_rope loop; csa_kernels has no RoPE/qk-norm batched twin. amp_dtype=bf16 requires an Ampere-or-newer GPU (exp_lib._active_amp refuses bf16 on pre-Ampere cards rather than silently changing the numerical path); amp_grad_scaler is false for bf16.
implementation_binding_provenance: predicted by exp_lib._uses_batched_eager + make_layer_cfgs and checked against every P5T record's real train_knobs; `python v12_supp.py plan` exercises the same admission path on synthetic records WITHOUT reading test data.
training_recipe: P3MT/P4MT/P5C: 3000 steps, seq 512, batch 12 (18.4M tokens consumed per run over the 8M-token train cache; identical data order per seed), all six arms under one config; csa_fixed_rope & full_rope via P3MT/P4MT (seeds 0-5) + P5C (seeds 6-11); full_rope_sink / csa_fixed_rope_nosink / csa_fixed_rope_randidx_seeded / csa_fixed_rope_allblocks via P5C (seeds 0-11, same recipe and outdir).

binding.training_recipe_note: Machine-checkable subset of the run_cfg fingerprint (keys as decoded by exp_lib.run_cfg_knobs). mt/det/df/cs are deliberately NOT pinned: they bind variant/environment/data/code and are verified separately (_code stamp, data_fp, manifest sha). v3 pins the parameter-matching knob mr per arm (binding.per_arm_recipe_signature): the shared signature cannot express one value for four arms because full_rope must be widened to mr=6.76348876953125 while the three csa arms stay at mr=4. Any record whose recipe fails this signature (including the per-arm mr) is refused by the confirmation statistics entry.

training_data_fingerprint.fingerprint_rule: exp_lib._ids_fp over the served 1-D train ids (train_fp on every checkpoint and training record)
training_data_fingerprint.binding_rule: if canonical_train_fp is a non-null string, every checkpoint and every admissible record must match it; otherwise all frozen checkpoints/records must agree on ONE non-null train_fp, which the first P5T access writes into results_lm_test/.freeze_lock.json and every later run must match. Mixed or missing train_fp is a hard refusal.
training_data_fingerprint.note: The literal value is intentionally not guessed here: it becomes checkable only against a built wt103_cache. Until then the run derives it from the frozen checkpoints BEFORE the first test read and locks it; a later change of training corpus is rejected.

test_slice.fingerprint_rule: exp_lib._ids_fp over the flattened (n_seqs, seq_len) rows; every record must carry the same non-null data_fp; the first P5T access writes it into results_lm_test/.freeze_lock.json

tokenizer.fit: same deterministic BPE fit as load_wikitext (first <=50k TRAIN rows only, vocab 8192)
tokenizer.check: load_wikitest hard-compares the full id->token vocabulary against the cached train tokenizer AND the persisted tokenizer bytes (sha256 recorded in test_meta) on every cache hit; a mismatch is a hard refusal, not a warning

checkpoint.stamp: v11.128 (= exp_lib.CODE_SEMANTICS; records carry _code, ckpt carries code)
checkpoint.hash: sha256 of the .pt file, stored per record as ckpt_sha256 at P5T evaluation time

binding.per_arm_recipe_signature_note: v5: full_rope_sink mr = full_rope mr - 48/(2*d*d*L) = 6.763427734375 (the learned sink adds n_heads*n_layers=48 parameters); csa_nosink and the seeded random arm are mr=4.0. The legacy fixed-hash randidx arm is retired from the frozen panel: its one global pattern is not a random variable across seeds, so it cannot support a selection-mechanism claim.

eval.data: wiki.test.raw via exp_lib.load_wikitest (held out; the ONLY phase allowed to read it)
eval.per_document: v5: 48 frozen test documents (up from 16). 48 < the code's 64-document population-claim floor and <64 is unavoidable at L4096 on WikiText-103 (~245k test tokens / 4097 ~= 59 non-overlapping rows); population claims stay refused, but the document-sampling readout is based on 48 units instead of 16.

scope.confirmatory_claims: ONLY fixed-chunk CSA claims: (a) learned top-k selection vs a seeded equal-budget random control, (b) sparse length extrapolation vs full RoPE attention, (c) block-compression/KV-projection effects at L4096, and (d) the pre-registered sink-matched / no-sink 2x2 sensitivity contrasts. Dynamic chunking, HCA and dynamic-boundary semantics are NOT covered.
scope.not_covered: dynamic chunking vs fixed chunking, semantic value of dynamic boundaries, HCA advantages, and dynamic-chunking scaling laws are NOT covered by this confirmation (no dynamic arm, no HCA comparison is frozen here). Also NOT covered: a sink-matched dense arm, an equal-read-budget all-block control, and population-level inference beyond the 16 frozen evaluation documents (n=16 < the code's 64-document population-claim floor).
scope.required_for: those claims require their own pre-registered freeze (arms, seeds, endpoints) before their first test-split access; until then they stay exploratory regardless of how the fixed-chunk confirmation turns out. A mechanism claim for the main contrast additionally requires the sink/kernel/qk-norm-matched and read-budget-matched controls described above.
scope.mechanism_claim_policy: v5: only the seeded-randidx-vs-learned contrast is eligible for a selection-mechanism claim, and only versus that seeded fixed pattern (not a fresh per-forward draw). main/aligned-dense/sink-matched/no-sink are system-level: the learned sink, kernel, qk-norm/kv-norm width and MLP width/FLOPs differ, and the sparse arm reads a ~256-token local span at L4096. allblocks is not read-budget matched (32x). The 2x2 is a sensitivity design, not a single-factor mechanism proof.

compute_budget_disclosure.parameter_matching: full_rope is param-matched to csa_fixed_rope by widening its MLP to mr=6.76348876953125 (11,089,904 vs 11,088,512, 0.013% apart); full_rope_sink uses mr=6.763427734375 because the learned sink adds 48 parameters (11,088,560). csa_fixed_rope_nosink removes the 48 sink parameters (11,089,856). This is capacity reallocation, not compute matching.
compute_budget_disclosure.flops: per-token training FLOPs of the dense reference are about 1.87x the csa arm (2.30M vs 1.23M: MLP +69%, attention 3.2x at L512).
compute_budget_disclosure.read_fraction: learned csa reads 32/128 = 25% of blocks at train L512 and 32/1024 = 3.1% at eval L4096; dense reads 100%; allblocks reads 128 blocks at L512 and 1024 at L4096.
compute_budget_disclosure.kernel: csa arms use the manual _rope_attn path (explicit -inf mask + split softmax); full_rope uses SDPA and switches backend between bf16 training and fp32 eval.
compute_budget_disclosure.reporting_rule: REPORT_v12.md and any paper table must state these caveats next to the comparison names; do not describe the main comparison as 'sparse vs dense at equal compute'.

primary_comparisons.name: main: csa_fixed_rope - full_rope @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: csa_fixed_rope better (negative delta) would confirm the sparse length-extrapolation advantage seen on validation
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: NOT a single-factor contrast. The dense reference is parameter-matched by widening its MLP to mr=6.76348876953125 (hidden 1731 vs 1024, +69% MLP width); per-token training FLOPs are therefore ~1.87x the csa arm (MLP +69%, attention 3.2x at L512). csa_fixed_rope reads 32/128 blocks at train L512 (25%) and 32/1024 at eval L4096 (3.1%), while full_rope reads 100%. The comparison also changes the attention kernel (manual _rope_attn vs SDPA), q_norm (extra F.normalize), kv_norm width (256 vs 32) and the learned sink (full_rope has full_sink=False). Report all four differences, not just 'parameter-matched dense'.
primary_comparisons.claim_note: Multi-factor system comparison (MLP width/FLOPs, kernel, qk-norm/kv-norm, sink, read fraction). v5 keeps it as the system-level headline; the sink-matched contrast below tests whether the sink difference explains it.

primary_comparisons.name: control: csa_fixed_rope_randidx_seeded - csa_fixed_rope @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: positive delta would confirm that learned selection beats a TRAINED random selector at equal read budget; the seeded arm draws a per-(seed, layer) pseudo-random pattern, so the control is a random variable across seeds
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: v5: the control is a per-(seed, layer) pseudo-random draw (salt = seed*1000003 + layer), not one global fixed hash; it remains deterministic for a given checkpoint and has the same dead W_DQ/W_DK/W_w parameters (~1.8% fewer effective parameters). The claim is learned selection vs this seeded random pattern at matched top-k, not vs a fresh draw at every forward.
primary_comparisons.claim_note: The only frozen comparison that may be read as selection-mechanism evidence. Narrow scope: it is a seeded pseudo-random pattern (not a fresh per-forward draw) and the arm has ~1.8% fewer effective parameters.

primary_comparisons.name: control: csa_fixed_rope_allblocks - csa_fixed_rope @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: positive delta would confirm that learned top-32 selection beats TRAINED all-block reading (allblocks reads strictly more information; this is a selection-vs-full-read contrast, NOT an equal-budget contrast)
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: v3 CORRECTS the v2 'at equal budget' wording: the arms are parameter-matched but NOT computation/reading-budget matched. index_topk=1000000, and lightning_indexer internally caps k=min(topk, B): allblocks reads 128 blocks at train L512 and 1024 blocks at eval L4096, versus 32 for learned (about 32x more at L4096). It is therefore an information-rich 'read everything' control, which is scientifically valid but must not be described as equal budget. The indexer's STE soft prior also differs (log(1/32) vs log(1/1024) on the selected set), so the learned sink strength differs by about 30x at L4096; 'only index_topk changed' is not accurate.
primary_comparisons.claim_note: Not reading-budget matched (32x at L4096); it is an information-rich upper bound, not an equal-budget control.

primary_comparisons.name: aligned-dense: full_rope_sink - csa_fixed_rope_allblocks @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: sink-matched dense-style reading vs standard dense attention (both arms now have a learned sink); non-directional mechanism readout
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: v5: both arms now have a learned sink, so the sink confound is removed from this readout. The kernel (SDPA vs manual _rope_attn), qk-norm/kv-norm width and read budget still differ; it remains a system-level mechanism readout, not a single-factor test.
primary_comparisons.claim_note: Sink-matched now, but kernel/qk-norm/kv-width/read-budget still differ; non-directional system-level readout.

primary_comparisons.name: sink-matched: csa_fixed_rope - full_rope_sink @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: negative delta would show the CSA advantage survives when the dense reference has the same learned sink; a positive delta would identify the sink as the explanation of the v4 main result
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: v5 sink-matched system comparison: sink, MLP/FLOPs, kernel, qk-norm/kv-norm and read fraction still differ. It is not a single-factor mechanism test; it is the pre-registered check of whether the v4 main contrast is a sink artifact.
primary_comparisons.claim_note: Removes the sink difference only; still multi-factor. Use it to interpret the main result, not as a mechanism claim.

primary_comparisons.name: no-sink: csa_fixed_rope_nosink - full_rope @ L4096 (test)
primary_comparisons.hypothesis_direction: negative delta would show the CSA advantage also holds in the no-sink cell of the 2x2; together with sink-matched it gives the sink-by-architecture difference-in-differences
primary_comparisons.interpretation_caveat: v5 no-sink cell: MLP/FLOPs, kernel, qk-norm/kv-norm and read fraction still differ. Compare its delta with the sink-matched delta; the difference is the sink-by-architecture interaction.
primary_comparisons.claim_note: No-sink cell of the 2x2; still multi-factor. The interaction is (csa_sink - full_sink) - (csa_nosink - full_rope), reported descriptively.

statistics.test: exact two-sided sign-flip over paired per-seed deltas
statistics.min_seeds_note: v5: with two-sided exact sign-flip and Holm/6, 8 seeds give a minimum attainable Holm p of 6*2/2^8 = 0.046875 < 0.05; the declared floor stays 8, but the shipped v5 requires all 12 seeds via require_complete_coverage=true.
statistics.min_consistency_note: v5: 11 is a SUFFICIENT condition under the equal-magnitude symbol-test projection, NOT the minimum for the exact sign-flip test. For unequal |delta| the exact test can reject with fewer same-sign seeds (e.g. 8x(+100) and 4x(-1): exact p=0.0078; Holm/6 p=0.047). It is recorded for reference and is not used as a decision threshold.
statistics.power_note: q = probability that a single seed's paired delta falls in the pre-registered direction. The table is computed by exp_lib.signflip_power, which implements the SYMBOL-TEST projection 2*P(Bin(n,1/2) <= n-k), NOT the exact sign-flip test that finaltest_stats actually runs. It is neither a design guarantee nor a rigorous bound in either direction: for unequal magnitudes the exact test can be more powerful (8/12 can suffice), and it can be less powerful when contrary deltas are large. Use it only as a rough design aid. Before the first test access, simulate sign-flips on the P5C per-seed validation delta vector (fixed |d_i|, enumerate 2^12 sign patterns) to obtain the real power / minimum same-sign count for THIS panel; if that power is inadequate, add seeds and record the revision in revision.history BEFORE touching test.
statistics.validity_assumptions: the exact sign-flip p requires within-seed exchangeability: both arms of a pair share everything stochastic except the arm itself (identical per-seed data order over the shared cache, same eval rows, same corruption grid; init RNG is seeded per seed -- architecture-induced RNG consumption differences are part of the arm). Seed-number equality alone does not provide this; see design_notes section 20. Machine-checked: data_fp, train_fp, n_seq, recipe, _code, manifest sha. Reported but NOT enforced: rng_fp (analysis writes validity.rng_fp_values / same_rng_fp).
statistics.decision_rule: A comparison is CONFIRMED only if p_holm < 0.05 AND its direction matches the validation-panel estimate AND param_matched is not false AND at least min_seeds_for_confirmation=8 complete pairs entered the test AND coverage_ok is true (v5; all 12 seeds) AND the pre-test power gate passed (or V12_ALLOW_LOW_POWER=1 is recorded). mechanism_claim_allowed=false comparisons are system-level and may not be written as mechanism evidence. Otherwise the claim stays exploratory.
statistics.seed_policy: seeds 0-11 fixed above; no seeds may be added after the first test-split evaluation (adding seeds after seeing results is selection bias by construction). Missing or incomplete seeds are reported as-is (smaller honest n_effective, never topped up); the declared floor is 8 complete pairs. The load-time power gate refuses any future manifest whose min attainable Holm p at that floor exceeds alpha. v4: because coverage is required for a confirmed verdict, a missing seed cannot be replaced by a smaller-n confirmation; the panel is reported as unconfirmed.
statistics.require_complete_coverage_note: v4 (review 5): every frozen seed must enter the comparison before it can be CONFIRMED. The 8-pair floor remains the mathematical resolution floor and is still reported, but a complete-case subset selected by wall-clock skips, missing checkpoints or the health gate is not random attrition. A partial panel is reported as descriptive/unconfirmed, never as a smaller-n confirmation.
statistics.power_gate_note: v4 (review 5): before the first test access, `python v12_supp.py power` enumerates the 2^12 sign patterns of the P5C per-seed validation deltas and reports the exact conditional power and the minimum same-sign count for THIS panel. The hard gate uses q=0.95 (the manifest's own design point at which 12 seeds reach 0.882 symbol-test power); q=0.90 is still reported as the realistic sensitivity and is expected to be ~0.66 at n=12. If power at q=0.95 is below min_power_for_test the driver refuses P5T; add seeds and record a revision before touching test (V12_ALLOW_LOW_POWER=1 is the explicit override).

history.change: review-5 methodological and engineering hardening, still BEFORE any test-split access. (1) statistics.require_complete_coverage=true: a complete-case subset (cap skips / missing checkpoints / health-gate refusals) can no longer be CONFIRMED as a smaller-n panel; the 8-pair mathematical floor is still reported. (2) Pre-test power gate: a zero-GPU exact conditional power calibration on the P5C validation deltas (`v12_supp.py power`) is now part of the frozen plan; P5T refuses when power at q=0.95 is below 0.8 (q=0.90 is still reported as the realistic sensitivity) unless explicitly overridden and recorded. (3) Claim-scope flags per primary comparison: only the randidx-vs-learned contrast may be read as selection-mechanism evidence, and even that only versus a fixed pseudo-random pattern; the main/aligned-dense contrasts are system-level. (4) Every admitted comparison now carries the full by-length curve (L512..L4096) as descriptive evidence, so an in-distribution reversal cannot be hidden behind the L4096 endpoint. (5) P5H health gate: a flat cosine tail (underfitting_or_stalled) is non-blocking and recorded; only nonfinite / overfitting / validation_degrading / insufficient_data / unmonitored block the test. (6) Driver phase order is P5C -> P5H -> P5PW -> P5T -> exploratory panels; a budget stop now reports INCOMPLETE and never prints ALL PHASES DONE. (7) The scheduled continuous-loop workflow is disabled (workflow_dispatch only) and the fast_prompt() unbounded-edit wrapper was removed.
